verdict.rationale: Snowflake documents several first-party programmatic surfaces. The REST APIs offer "end-to-end automation" of resources, with OpenAPI specs. The SQL API can run any SQL statement and "manage your deployment" (users, roles, tables). Snowflake CLI covers apps, and Cortex Analyst is exposed via REST. Together these cover the core of the story, but nothing in the evidence states parity with the Snowsight UI, and UI-centric features such as dashboards and notebooks have no stated API equivalent. missing for 10: an explicit documented API/UI parity guarantee, evidence that Snowsight-only features (dashboards, notebook authoring, activity views) are API-accessible, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: The Snowflake REST APIs suite of APIs enables developers to build end-to-end automation and integration with Snowflake resources.
You can use this API to develop custom applications and integrations that: Perform queries, Manage your deployment (e.g. provision users and roles, create tables, etc.)
Snowflake REST APIs for resource management provide a set of endpoints that lets users programmatically interact with and control various resources within the Snowflake Data Cloud.
These REST APIs are compliant with the OpenAPI specification.
Available as a convenient REST API, Cortex Analyst can be seamlessly integrated into any application.
